boundary_condition: If a connecting itinerary is considered for savings, keep the stop tolerance low by allowing only one layover rather than multiple stops.
condition: When comparing flight itineraries for a typical trip and no special comfort or major price-saving reason favors a stop.
default_action: Prioritize nonstop flights before connecting itineraries.
exception_condition: For very long coast-to-coast-style flights where the traveler wants a break, look for a midway stopover instead of forcing nonstop.
name: Default to nonstop flights when practical
preference_value: nonstop by default, with limited exceptions for cost or long-flight comfort
rationale: Most independent examples state or imply that nonstop is preferred, including 'non-stop is always preferred,' 'definitely a non-stop,' and 'a nonstop flight.' One example allows a layover when it is cheaper but limits it to one layover, and another requests a midway stopover for coast-to-coast travel. Together, these support a scoped synthetic habit: default to nonstop when practical, but allow a single layover for savings or a stopover for long-flight comfort.
